scope: One job per separately spawned Rust worker; shared std-only binary codec. Process separation is not an OS sandbox.

frame.sequence: Independent direction counters start0 and increase exactly once; reject duplicates, gaps and wrap.
frame.payload: Fixed enum tags and LE integers; length-prefix byte/string/vector values with allocation bounds; reject unknown tags and trailing fields.

paths.rules: Platform encoding must match. Reject NUL and nonabsolute roots; Windows UNC/device paths unsupported. No lossy execution paths.
paths.archive_names: Separate validated UTF-8 relative names; entry IDs are opaque ordinal u32, not paths.

commands.Start: Exactly once: List{archive}, Extract{archive,destination,selection:All|EntryIds{ids:[u32]},list_id:optional<ListId>,gzip_output_name:optional<UTF8>}, CreateZip{sources:[source_path,archive_name],output_file,method:Store|Deflate,encryption:None|Aes256}. App supplies job_id; caller can lower worker hard limits. Extract destination is always an absolute output directory. EntryIds requires list_id; All may supply list_id to bind extraction to a displayed list.
commands.Password: Matching outstanding challenge_id:u64 and max1024 UTF-8 bytes; never log, Debug, echo or persist secrets.
commands.Cancel: Matching header job_id and empty body; command header sequence identifies the request. See CancelAck. Request acceptance is separate from final outcome. EOF alone is not successful cancellation.

events.Accepted: Action and capabilities; encryption capability remains false until implementation and verification are complete.
events.Entry: entry_id, name, kind File|Directory|Link|Other, declared sizes, encrypted; ordinal u32 IDs belong to this List job only until its ListEnd token and Completed Terminal are confirmed. Metadata only, no CRC success claim.
events.ListEnd: entry_count:u32 and list_id:ListId for a complete listing. Entry IDs are deterministic zero-based ordinals in archive traversal order. App associates this token with this job entries only after Completed Terminal, both stream EOFs and successful child wait/exit.
events.PasswordRequired: challenge_id, attempt and purpose Decrypt|Encrypt; no secret diagnostics.
events.Output: entry_id:optional, relative_name, disposition Created|PartialRetained|Removed|CommitUncertain; only this job outputs.

Terminal.detail: Bounded local description, not a substitute for typed errors.

CancelAck.request_sequence: u64: echoed Cancel command header sequence; separate from this event header sequence.
CancelAck.Requested: Cancellation flag was latched for the first time before the job cancellation cutoff. Cooperative request acceptance; not a guarantee of Cancelled, no outputs or rollback.
CancelAck.AlreadyRequested: Cancellation was already latched and the job can still observe it. The flag stays latched; no second request or reset.
CancelAck.TooLate: Final job completion/commit decision has been sealed so cancellation can no longer influence the outcome; final outcome may still be Failed or publication Uncertain. Previously created entries alone do not make a multi-entry job TooLate.
CancelAck.Finished: Business outcome has already been fixed, but Terminal has not yet been emitted. Does not establish success, EOF, child exit or reaping.
CancelAck.ordering: Each well-formed Cancel consumed before Terminal is acknowledged once before Terminal. Terminal is the last worker protocol frame. A Cancel racing with Terminal/exit may remain unread and have no acknowledgement; app uses Terminal plus EOF and wait, never synthesizes a worker acknowledgement or successful cancellation.

lifecycle: Start once; no automatic retry or overwrite. Password/Cancel remain readable during work.
Parent drains both streams concurrently. Stdout is protocol only; stderr is bounded diagnostics without secrets.

Exactly one Terminal ends business results and is the final worker protocol frame; CancelAck can precede but never follow it. Worker exits0 after delivered terminal, including Failed/Cancelled. Malformed protocol or crash can exit nonzero without terminal.
App requires matching terminal, stdout/stderr EOF and owned child wait/exit before replacement/close. EOF/exit0 alone is not success.
Lost/killed worker preserves observed outputs; unobserved commit/cleanup stays uncertain, never synthetic Cancelled/rollback/absent output.
Cancellation retains completed outputs; cleanup removes only owned temporary files and reports any retained partial.
Completed is not OS sandboxing or release evidence. No security-setting changes.
safe_output: Reject absolute/dotdot/drive/UNC/device/reserved/alternate-stream names and case/path collisions before writes.
Reject archive links/special entries on extraction. Do not follow output parent symlinks/reparse points.
Create output files exclusively; never truncate or write pre-existing files. GZip FNAME does not choose destination.
CRC/size/stream-end validation precedes committed output events; preserve commit/durability/cleanup distinctions.
pending: Frontend draft acceptance was conditional on these three clarifications, now specified. Shared codec and app/worker integration remain unimplemented and unverified.
RustCrypto version selection, encryption implementation and verification; capability remains unavailable until complete.
Actual Linux and Windows build/runtime results; neither claimed yet.

crypto.policy: Human approved pure Rust RustCrypto under MIT/Apache. No home-grown AES or password KDF; approval alone does not enable encryption capability.

coordination.basis: Frontend can use the draft subject to three clarifications. This revision specifies list identity, explicit raw GZip output naming and cancellation acknowledgement. It does not claim implementation or runtime verification.

ListId.catalog_version: u16=1; reject unsupported versions without remapping entry IDs.
ListId.format: ZIP|TAR|GZIP|TAR_GZIP; detected parser mode, not the filename extension.
ListId.source_object: Tagged native identity from the opened source handle: Unix{device:u64,inode:u64} or Windows{volume_serial:u64,file_id:[u8;16]}. Platform must match; unavailable reliable identity returns UnsupportedFeature.
ListId.archive_bytes: u64: exact complete compressed/source byte length, bounded by worker limits.
ListId.archive_sha256: [u8;32]: SHA-256 of every source byte, using the permitted RustCrypto implementation; not CRC or path/size/mtime alone.

capture: Open the regular source file once and keep its handle. Copy through bounded reads into a private job-owned snapshot while computing full SHA-256. Check source handle identity, length and modification metadata before/after capture; detected mutation rejects the capture. Check the named source still resolves to the same object at the validation boundary.

The completed private snapshot is the sole input to parsing and decoding for this job; never hash one file and later reopen the path to decode. Snapshot storage is bounded, exclusively owned and not writable through attacker-selected names. Failure to establish a stable private snapshot fails before creating destination outputs.
List builds the deterministic catalog from that snapshot and returns its ListId only with successful ListEnd. A failed/cancelled/truncated listing provides no reusable selection token.
extract_validation: Treat every supplied ListId and entry ID as untrusted. EntryIds without ListId, empty/duplicate IDs or IDs outside the recomputed catalog fail InvalidRequest before destination output creation.

Capture the Extract source into a new private snapshot, recompute identity/length/SHA-256/format/catalog version and compare every ListId field before creating any destination output. A mismatch returns Terminal Failed/SourceChanged with publication None and zero created/retained outputs. The app invalidates the displayed selection and asks the user to reopen/list; no automatic extraction retry or ordinal remapping.
When All supplies ListId, apply the same comparison. All without ListId means extract the current captured archive without claiming it matches any earlier listing.

EntryIds refer to the recomputed catalog ordinals, never names supplied by the app; extract the selected members in archive traversal order. Link/special-entry and output path guards remain mandatory after identity validation.
list_identity.boundary: This binds extraction to verified snapshot bytes and observed native identity at capture/validation time. It is not authorization, a signed token, an exclusive filesystem lock or a promise to detect every external edit after capture or a byte-identical change-and-restore. Later source changes cannot change the bytes decoded from the private snapshot.

gzip_output.destination: Always the output directory, never a full output filename.
gzip_output.gzip_output_name: Required Some(nonempty validated UTF-8 single leaf filename) for raw GZIP extraction, for both All and EntryIds. Reject absolute/drive/UNC/device/alternate-stream/reserved names, separators, dot/dotdot and invalid leaf names before creating outputs. Missing/invalid value returns InvalidRequest; no implicit basename or FNAME fallback.
gzip_output.other_formats: Must be None for ZIP, TAR and TAR_GZIP; reject Some as InvalidRequest rather than silently ignoring it. TAR_GZIP uses validated inner TAR member names.
gzip_output.gzip_catalog: Raw GZIP is one logical stream entry with entry_id0. Its listed display name is not an output path; entry selection still requires ListId.
gzip_output.publication: Resolve the supplied leaf under destination using the same no-follow and exclusive-create guards. Existing destination files return Conflict; never overwrite, rename to an automatic alternative or retry.

design_references.purpose: RustCrypto SHA-256 implementation documentation; dependency version and advisories still require selection-time verification.
Source metadata from the open file descriptor rather than a later path reopen.

seven_zip_extension.compatibility: Existing format values 0 through 3, fields, message tags and frame version stay unchanged. Older clients reject format 4. App Format and bidirectional conversion require an update.
seven_zip_extension.regression: Preserve existing format bytes and round-trip SevenZip in ListEnd/ListId.
